topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and susceptibility to mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutations can produce cancer through clonal evolution and explain why some cells and individuals are more susceptible.

topics.label: Assessing the environmental contribution to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence and uncertainty involved in attributing cancer to environmental exposures rather than treating it as inevitable bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental agents become mutagenic through their interactions with DNA and cellular processes.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutation-producing initiation from promotion that enables altered cells to proliferate in a supportive environment.

topics.label: Context-dependent carcinogen susceptibility and mechanistic summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics complete the mechanistic account by explaining developmental susceptibility and summarising how carcinogen effects depend on biological context.

topics.label: Human evidence linking carcinogen exposure to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence obtained from human tumours and populations can connect particular exposures with cancer.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate controlled experimental tests of carcinogenic potential and explain why their results may not fully capture cancer risk in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its main conclusions and placing cancer risks within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
